ios.desc:
Welcome to Daily Philosophy, a haven for thinkers and seekers alike. Our app offers a daily dose of philosophical wisdom, guiding you on a journey through the minds of history's greatest thinkers. Immerse yourself in a world where ancient wisdom meets modern reflection, tailored for the curious soul.

What's Inside:
• Daily Wisdom: Start each day with compelling quotes from renowned philosophers.
• Philosopher Profiles: Explore the lives, eras, and impactful ideas of philosophical legends.
• Journey Through Time: Travel from the Ancient world to the Enlightenment in our time period collections.
• Explore Concepts: Over 30 philosophical topics, including Aristotle’s Ethics and Descartes' Cogito.
• Reflective Practice: Daily reflections rooted in philosophies from Stoicism to Buddhism.
• Meditative Visuals: Enhance your reflection with serene, animated visuals.
• Philosophical Widgets: Adorn your screen with daily quotes for a burst of inspiration.

Key Features:
• Curated Content: Rich, thoughtfully selected content for daily engagement.
• Interactive Exploration: Dive into philosophy with an interactive and engaging interface.
• Tranquil Meditation: Unique visuals for a complete, peaceful meditative experience.

Why Choose Daily Philosophy?
Daily Philosophy isn't just an app; it's a companion on your path to personal growth and intellectual exploration. It's designed for anyone who seeks meaning in the everyday, offering a unique mix of historical wisdom and contemporary reflection techniques. Transform your daily routine into a journey of self-discovery and mindful learning.
Download Daily Philosophy now and embark on a journey of enlightenment, one day at a time.

quotes.text:
My collection of art, philosophy and poetry apps. They have previously just been on iOS but I just finished the Kotlin port of the art one, so will be releasing that soon.

The poetry one is react native. Art and philosophy ones are swift/kotlin. I wanted to see if you could use LLMs to effectively create a cross-platform app. The idea behind react native was that you write it once in an approachable language, then the framework compiles to native app code. In 2025, the approachable language you code in is English, and the LLM now generates native app code.

It was generally a success and I feel less of a need of the development overhead of react native these days.

quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (May 2025)

quotes.text: GPT is a game changer. My new mantra, and what I've been telling developer friends, is "Don't build one side project, build twelve." I realised that this is effectively what VCs do, where they'll often have a portfolio of companies, even if they only expect one of them to net a 100x return. It was also inspired by reading success stories on IndieHackers, where I noticed a common theme was someone saying "this is the 6th product I've released, and I finally landed on something that got big." I further think that GPT unlocks the capability to move at this speed, it helped me spec out features, then write the actual code for them. Previously I have only released React Native apps, as I was more familiar with React in my professional job. Being able to describe what I want, and then have the SwiftUI code be generated for me, was remarkable! I have a further selection of ideas which I'll be building, and would thoroughly recommend to other devs that they start leveraging these tools. I might consolidate these thoughts a bit further in a future blog post.
